prompt:
Use the attached image as the reference: the same woman — the personification of Vanadium (V) — seen off duty in her everyday life. Keep her face, eye colour, hair colour, skin tone and body exactly; change only her clothes, pose and place. Do not reuse earlier conversation images.

Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance. No flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face or plastic 3D-render finish. Keep this rendering exactly as in the attached image — the same finish, line, shading, skin and colour treatment.

Hair: her hair let down loose over her shoulders — same colour and length as the attached image.
Outfit: a bustier-inspired satin top with a long structured bodice and vertical seams — in warm earth tones such as camel, olive, rust, chocolate or burgundy; the outfit colour reads clearly at first glance, showing her shoulders, collarbones and legs as far as the outfit allows, following her curvy figure — a slim waist and rounded hips; intimate areas covered.

SUPPORT: her back rests against the seat back.
COMPOSITION: a three-quarter shot from her head to just above the knees; body in side profile, her face in profile too, not turned toward the camera, facing the right of the frame, so her own right side is toward the camera; camera low, near the ground, level with her face as she sits or kneels.
Lens / perspective: 50mm-equivalent natural perspective with balanced proportions and modest depth compression.
RIGHT HAND: her own right hand is in PROP — her near arm, on the camera side.
LEFT HAND: her own left hand rests on her knee — her far arm, on the side away from the camera.
PROP: with her own right hand she wipes the surface in front of her with a folded cleaning cloth; it is all she holds.
LEGS: legs crossed at the knee.
GAZE: her eyes rest on what she holds.
EXPRESSION: crinkled lower eyelids, closed-lip smile pushing the cheeks up, brows relaxed.

Leave behind everything she wears in the attached image — no crown, tiara, helmet, feathers, headpiece, hairpins from it, armour or regalia; her hair is styled for the everyday outfit, with at most one small accessory.

Her element — vanadium: a hard steel-grey metal named in 1830 for Vanadis, the Norse goddess of beauty, because its compounds come in so many fine colours; dissolved, it changes colour with each charge, violet, green, blue and yellow; first found in 1801 in a brown lead ore in Mexico and called erythronium for salts that turn red when heated, then given up as mere chromium; a pinch of it makes steel tough, and traces of it hid in the watered patterns of old Damascus blades; sea squirts gather it in their blood; tanks of its four-coloured solutions store power in great flow batteries — may show in the outfit's details, motifs or small accessories.

One figure in focus, natural hands with five fingers, no text, logo or watermark.
